quote: But I ask no favors for my sex. I surrender not our claim to equality. All I ask of our brethren is, that they will take their feet from off our necks, and permit us to stand upright on that ground which God designed us to occupy.
source: Sarah Moore Grimké, Letters on the Equality of the Sexes, Letter II, Woman Subject Only to God, p. 10 (Isaac Knapp, 1838)

evidence.where: Full text of the 1838 Isaac Knapp printing at Project Gutenberg ebook 69485, produced from Internet Archive page images; the page marker Pg 10 falls in the sentence before the passage, so the whole quotation sits on p. 10
evidence.edition: Letters on the Equality of the Sexes, and the Condition of Woman, addressed to Mary S. Parker (Boston: Isaac Knapp, 1838)
evidence.locator: Letter II, Woman Subject Only to God, dated Newburyport, 7th mo. 17, 1837, p. 10

reason: Every word matches, including from off our necks, which the shortened popular version drops. Letter heading, dateline, publisher and page are all as proposed. Grimké stands at one of three for the year and appears once in this month.
